The uncommitted working-tree edit of common.rs (line 899: max raw_score) gives NCBI's order when nothing is dropped, but is wrong once a query has more than N subjects with hits: then NCBI's order of the kept subjects is the e-value state (tie3.fa N=2: NCBI SB SA). The port must pass, per query, whether the hit list overflowed (heapified) and use the max raw score if not, else the first HSP's score after the e-value sort. Impact low: only exact ties of best e-value (equal doubles, or both < 1e-180).

tblastx_behavior: With -culling_limit the preliminary writer is the culling writer: HSPs go into culling trees and s_BlastHSPCullingFinal (hspfilter_culling.c:501-593) fills the query hit lists with ALL surviving subjects (no Blast_HitListUpdate, no cut at N; lists sorted by score, best_evalue = minimum). A traceback-stage pipe (s_BlastHSPCullingPipeRun, 699-730) culls again and re-sorts. The cut at N then happens in the traceback stage's Blast_HSPResultsInsertHSPList, the final HSP lists are score-sorted by the pipe (Final), and the final subject sort sees the score state whatever the overflow.
notes: UNSURE: only two oracle runs: tie3.fa and tie3c.fa with -culling_limit 100: N=1 -> SB / SA (kept subject same as without culling), N=2 -> SA SB (score state) in both, whereas without culling tie3.fa N=2 gives SB SA. The rest of the culling path (which HSPs survive, e-values of culled lists) belongs to the culling inventory.
